import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create the FacetGrid
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',
    y='survived',
    hue='who',
    col='alone',
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis',
    height=6,
    aspect=0.8,
    legend=False,
    order=['First', 'Second', 'Third']
)

# Set a comprehensive title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Rate: Class, Demographics, and Traveling Companions',
               fontsize=18, y=1.03)

# Iterate through the axes to customize labels and formatting
for i, ax in enumerate(g.axes.flat):
    # Set a more descriptive Y-axis label
    ax.set_ylabel('Survival Rate')
    
    # Format Y-axis as percentage
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
    
    # Set custom titles for each subplot (column)
    if i == 0:
        ax.set_title('Traveling with Family')
    else:
        ax.set_title('Traveling Alone')
        
    # Set X-axis label
    ax.set_xlabel('Passenger Class')

    # Add data labels on top of each bar
    for p in ax.patches:
        ax.annotate(f'{p.get_height():.0%}',
                    (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                    ha='center', va='center',
                    xytext=(0, 9),
                    textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=9,
                    color='dimgray')

# Adjust layout and add a single legend for the figure
plt.legend(title='Passenger Type', loc='upper right')
g.fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
